correctness.rationale: Reconstructed Hall neighbor sets for the four index masks (0,p,q,pq), proving the exact four inequalities without any progression assumption. Primitive residue pairs modulo each r>=5 are uniformly distributed over r^2-1 nonzero pairs; each index has hit probability 1/(r+1), an empty support probability (r-3)/(r+1). Inclusion-exclusion gives U and W, and the 12 forbidden pairs of two-element subsets yield the subtraction. CRT and coprime Möbius inversion for fixed pq give the stated finite-H error; the k asymptotic follows by comparing exponential bases. Independently enumerated all 256 index-mask patterns, tested dynamic local-support laws for p,q=(5,7),(5,11),(7,11), k<=5 and confirmed k=2 success densities 47/48,107/108,191/192. The fixed-(p,q,k) quantifiers and p,q>=5 boundary are essential; do not extend the density to primes 2 or 3.

final_claim: For any fixed distinct primes p<q at least 5 and every k>=1, the proportion of k separately primitive positive four-term arithmetic progressions admitting one SAME coprime bijection to divisors {1,p,q,pq} is U_p(k) U_q(k) - 12 W_p(k) W_q(k), with the exact four-index Hall criterion, H^{2k} density counting error O(H^{2k-1}log H), and sharp k->infinity coefficient 24.
